subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Is Dark Roast Stronger?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Is Dark Roast Stronger?.

hook.text: Most people believe dark roast is 'stronger'—more caffeine, more intensity. The truth is the opposite.

buildup.text: Dark roast beans are larger (expanded by heat) and lighter (moisture lost). Per scoop, you get fewer beans than light roast.

discovery.text: Caffeine is stable through roasting. But dark roast beans weigh less, so a scoop of dark has slightly less caffeine.

twist.text: What people perceive as 'strength' is actually bitter, smoky roast flavor—not caffeine content. Bold taste ≠ high caffeine.

climax.text: If measured by weight (grams), dark and light are nearly identical in caffeine. The myth comes from measuring by volume.

punchline.text: Dark roast tastes bold but isn't stronger. Flavor intensity fooled everyone.

quiz.question: Why does a scoop of dark roast have slightly less caffeine than light?
options: Dark beans are larger and lighter — fewer beans per scoop means less total caffeine
